name: Aakash Mishra
bio: I build medical imaging and language models at Epsilon Health, an AI-native radiology practice in San Francisco. Before that I spent three years at Meta, most recently as a senior machine learning engineer and area lead in Monetization. I studied computer science at Harvard and Stanford.

epsilon.blurb: Epsilon is an AI-native radiology practice. Our models support Epsilon's own radiologists as they read X-rays. I work on how those models see, explain and report.

points: Founding member of the research team behind an AI-native radiology practice.
Training and serving the imaging and report-generation models used by Epsilon's radiologists.
Published research on model explainability and X-ray preprocessing.

work.role: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, Area Lead
points: Area lead in Facebook Monetization. Started and shipped ML projects that reached billions of users.
First author on causal-informed online optimization for ad-load personalization, published at a NeurIPS 2025 workshop.
Trained a sentiment model to predict community response to proposed solar projects, fed by a pipeline that scraped town-hall notes and news.
Fine-tuned GPT-2 to summarize renewable-energy articles, and built a geospatial graph network to predict a project's effect on incident light.
Designed a framework that detects user-identifying information in ML training data, and automated privacy checks for model deployment.
Integrated a feature-engineering framework into the serving platform. Earned a return offer.
Built AWS EMR and S3 data infrastructure with Terraform, plus Ranger access control for Hive.
Wrote Airflow pipelines that moved terabytes of data to Salesforce through Kafka.
Built a Django REST API for DHCP and ARP network data, and a 3D view of over 10,000 intrusion alerts an hour.
Wrote parsers that organized more than 30 TB of security data.

education.degree: AB, Computer Science, summa cum laude
notes: Thesis with Stratos Idreos, Data Systems Lab

projects.title: Distributed Traffic Control
projects.text: Fault-tolerant traffic-light control with reinforcement learning agents that coordinate over gRPC, so the grid keeps working when some agents fail.

projects.title: PHOSS
projects.text: A simulator for distributed hyperparameter search. It generates synthetic loss landscapes so schedulers can be compared without training real models.

projects.title: RayICV
projects.text: Hyperparameter tuning with cross-validation built in, on top of Ray Train. Schedules jobs by fold and model configuration.

projects.title: Ray PowerSGD
projects.text: A Ray-based all-reduce implementation of PowerSGD, the low-rank gradient compression method for distributed training.

projects.title: Boston Datathon winner
projects.text: A k-nearest-neighbors take on synthetic control over 70,000 NIH patient records. Showed a causal effect of glipizide on heart failure outcomes and won first place.

projects.title: Harvard RoboCup
projects.text: Robot soccer players that combine control, vision and strategy. I led the team and wrote both firmware and high-level strategy code.

projects.title: NoetherAutoDiff
projects.text: An automatic differentiation library for differential-equation matrices written as text or LaTeX, usable from C++ and Python.

projects.title: dftoltx
projects.text: Turns pandas DataFrames into LaTeX table code.
